transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, it’s... I don't even really know where to start, honestly. I guess I came in because... well, lately I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up anymore. Just go to sleep and have that be the end of it. Every morning my alarm goes off at 4:30 because I do flooring, you know, carpet and tile installation, and the job sites open early. I went to college for a couple of years but I ended up in the trades, which used to be fine, but lately... I just lie there in the dark when that alarm goes off and think about how much easier it would be to just let go. 

And it’s not just that I’m tired of the grind, it’s... I really feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew. I’ve got these guys on my crew who depend on me to line up the jobs and keep the pace, and my family at home, and I just feel like I’m this massive burden dragging all of them down. Like I’ve let them all down so badly and ruined so much that the only way to make it right, the only just thing to do, is to just not be here anymore. I just keep running it over and over in my head while I'm working, just staring at the floor tiles thinking about how I deserve to be punished for it all, and how if I just didn't wake up tomorrow, it would finally balance the scales for them.
Do you believe with complete certainty that you have ruined things and deserve punishment, even when other people tell you that this isn’t true?

Yes. I mean, people try to say that it isn't true. My sister, or some of the guys on the crew, they'll say, "Hey, it's just a bad season," or "You're doing your best," but... they're just being nice, or they just don't see the whole picture like I do. Because I know. I know with absolute certainty. 

It’s like... well, you just have to look at my husband. I just keep thinking about how he got so much worse recently, his stress and everything, and I know it’s entirely because of me. If he had married someone else, someone who wasn't so destructive, he’d be fine right now. I just sucked the life right out of him, day after day. And it doesn't even stop at home, it bleeds into my work, too. We lost a whole string of contracts last month—good jobs, the kind that keep the guys fed through the winter—and the crew lost all that work because of me. I was the one doing the walk-throughs and the bidding, and I just... I ruined it. I drove the work away. 

Even the jobs we did finish, I look back at them and I just know I messed up those clients' homes. Like, these people save up for years, you know? They save up to get their tile redone, to make their house beautiful, their safe place, and I just went in there and ruined their spaces. It’s this heavy, awful feeling... it's like I have this actual poison on my hands. Like I literally poisoned everything I touched. My marriage, the guys' livelihoods, these strangers' houses. Everywhere I go, everything I get involved in just rots because of me. 

So, yeah, when people tell me I'm being too hard on myself, I just think they don't understand the sheer scale of what I've destroyed. I deserve whatever happens to me. I really do. If I lose everything, or if the absolute worst happens, it's exactly what I've earned for poisoning all these people's lives.
Have you ever had a previous period in your life when you felt this depressed and believed you deserved punishment?

Previous? I mean... it's not really a previous period, doctor, because it hasn't ever stopped. It's just been this one, long, endless stretch of time. This whole heavy, crushing feeling, this absolute certainty that I deserve to be punished... it’s been with me for about a year and two months now. It hasn't let up for a single day in all that time. 

I know exactly how long it’s been because it started just a few months after my husband's injury. See, he got hurt, and at first, right after it happened, we were just in survival mode. I was trying to juggle my flooring contracts, figuring out how to keep the crew moving on this big commercial lobby job we had just landed, while also dealing with his appointments and the sudden drop in our income. I was just running on adrenaline, I guess, just trying to keep the lights on and the guys working. 

But then, a few months after his injury... that's when the adrenaline ran out and this... this darkness just completely swallowed me whole. I remember I was laying out this intricate herringbone pattern on a floor, just staring at the grout lines, and it just hit me how much worse he was getting, and how it was all my fault. That was a year and two months ago. And ever since that day, I’ve just been carrying it. Every morning when that 4:30 alarm goes off, every night when I'm lying in the dark. It just goes on and on, this feeling that I ruined his life and I need to pay for it. So, no, it's not a past thing that went away and came back. It's just been this one continuous, year-and-two-month-long reality since shortly after he got hurt.
